records.name: Similarity preserves characteristic polynomial
records.statement: If B=P^{-1}AP for an invertible finite-dimensional change of basis P over R or C, then A and B have the same characteristic polynomial; therefore trace, determinant, and rank are preserved.
hypotheses: A and B are square matrices over R or C
nonclaims: Sharing a characteristic polynomial does not imply similarity in general.

records.name: Orthogonal or unitary similarity preserves Frobenius norm
records.statement: Orthogonal similarity over R and unitary similarity over C are similarity transformations and additionally preserve the Frobenius norm.
hypotheses: B=Q^T A Q with Q^TQ=I over R, or B=U^* A U with U^*U=I over C
nonclaims: Ordinary similarity need not preserve the Frobenius norm.

records.name: Invertible congruence preserves rank
records.statement: If B=P^TAP over R with P invertible, then rank(B)=rank(A); if A is symmetric then B is symmetric. Congruence does not generally preserve eigenvalues.
hypotheses: A is a real square matrix
nonclaims: Congruence is not spectral equivalence and is not interchangeable with similarity.

records.name: Coordinate change preserves abstract linear action
records.statement: For v'=P^{-1}v and A'=P^{-1}AP with P invertible, A'v'=P^{-1}(Av); the coordinate representation changes while the represented linear action is covariant.
nonclaims: Coordinate covariance does not establish physical equivalence of independently modelled systems.

records.name: Injective receiver re-encoding preserves observation equivalence
records.statement: For a deterministic observation O:S->Y and receiver map R:Y->Z that is injective on im(O), R(O(x))=R(O(y)) iff O(x)=O(y); hence the observation fibres are unchanged.
nonclaims: A noninjective receiver map may merge observation classes and therefore changes the observation equivalence relation.

records.name: Congruent need not be similar
records.statement: I2 and diag(4,1) are congruent via P=diag(2,1) but are not similar because their traces and characteristic polynomials differ.
nonclaims: The counterexample distinguishes equivalence notions only; it makes no physical claim.

records.name: Similar need not be orthogonally similar
records.statement: diag(1,2) is similar via a shear to [[1,-1],[0,2]], but their Frobenius norms differ, so they cannot be orthogonally similar.
nonclaims: Failure of orthogonal similarity does not refute ordinary similarity.

records.name: Same characteristic polynomial need not imply similarity
records.statement: I2 and the nontrivial Jordan block [[1,1],[0,1]] have the same characteristic polynomial but are not similar because rank(A-I) differs.
nonclaims: Characteristic-polynomial equality is a necessary similarity invariant, not a complete classifier.

records.name: Noninjective receiver re-encoding can merge fibres
records.statement: An observation distinguishing x0 and x1 can become indistinguishable after a receiver map sends both observation values to one output.
nonclaims: Receiver-induced merging is representation loss, not evidence of physical state merging.

records.name: Coordinate tuple alone does not identify an abstract vector
records.statement: The coordinate tuple (1,0) denotes different abstract vectors in the standard basis and in the swapped basis; the chart/basis is part of the representation.
nonclaims: This is a coordinate-identity counterexample, not a claim that abstract vectors lack identity.

claim_boundary: SIMILARITY != CONGRUENCE; COORDINATE_TUPLE != ABSTRACT_OBJECT; RECEIVER_REENCODING != STATE_TRANSFORMATION; FINITE_REPRESENTATION_CONFORMANCE != GENERAL_PROOF
